blocks.text:
I need to find the worst steric clash between two non-bonded residues, so I'm scanning for unusually short contacts by estimating spatial proximity across the chain, possibly organized into helices or loops, to identify suspicious pairs worth checking more closely.

Checking CYS A2034's SG position against nearby residues, I'm tracing the CA backbone path through residues 2002-2021 to map out the fold's trajectory in 3D space, which seems to move from one region and curve back around, helping me identify which residues might be spatially close despite being far apart in sequence.

Continuing through the coordinate sequence toward 2071, the trajectory resembles a coiled coil or long helical hairpin. I'm now scanning for non-adjacent contacts, wondering if the 2010-2015 strand and 2060-2063 strand come close in space based on similar x/y/z ranges.

Checking specific atom distances between residues 2034/2062 and their sidechains, none seem close enough to be meaningful contacts. I'm trying to systematically group the structure into three segments—roughly 2002-2020, 2021-2050, and 2051-2071—and check CA-CA distances under 6 Å across non-adjacent pairs, but none of the candidates I'm testing (2011/2060, 2043/2007, 2013/2045) are actually close. I'm now cross-checking residues in the 2002-2020 range against the 2040-2062 range for any tight spatial pairing.

Most of these pairs are too far apart to matter, though 2020 near 2025 and 2016 near 2030 look moderately close at ~6-7.5 Å. I'm now considering whether the actual clash involves a selenium atom in the MSE residue at 2060, checking its distance to nearby leucine sidechains—one at position 2038 comes out to about 5.0 Å, which seems worth pursuing further.

Checking the MSE selenium against more leucine carbons at 2037 gives distances around 4.2-4.9 Å, and I'm now comparing a cysteine sulfur at 2034 to nearby tyrosine and glutamate sidechains, finding roughly 4.8 Å—still not tight enough to flag. Looking at valine 2030's gamma carbons against leucine 2016's delta carbons, I get a closer distance of about 3.87 Å, which is borderline but probably acceptable for carbon-carbon contacts.

I'm now scanning other sidechain pairs—isoleucine 2033 against leucine 2029, isoleucine 2014 against leucine 2012—but these all come out too far apart to be clashes. Shifting focus to the region between residues 2030-2034 and 2062-2064, I'm starting to examine the tyrosine 2062 ring coordinates.

I found a tyrosine hydroxyl to threonine gamma carbon distance of about 3.3 Å, which is acceptable for an O...C contact, and similarly checked threonine's other oxygen against the same hydroxyl at 4.6 Å. Checking glutamate 2035's carboxylate against leucine 2038 gives roughly 3.65 Å, also not severe enough. Since none of these individual checks are turning up a true clash, I think I need a more systematic approach—grouping atoms into spatial bins to hunt for genuinely close pairs, since severe clashes in deposited structures often involve charged sidechain pairs like lysine and glutamate.

I'm now scanning coordinates region by region, checking side-chain tip atoms of leucine 2016, isoleucine, and valine residues for pairs with nearly identical positions, then moving to check valine 2043, phenylalanine 2045, and nearby serine and leucine residues for anything under 2.5 Å, but so far all distances I'm computing are too large to represent a real clash.

Since scanning residue by residue isn't converging, I'm switching strategy to systematically list every CA coordinate along the chain so I can compute pairwise distances between non-adjacent residues and quickly narrow down which pairs sit close enough in space to be worth examining for atomic clashes.

I'm scanning pairs of residues for close contacts, calculating distances between non-adjacent CA atoms to find ones under 8 angstroms. Several pairs stand out as potentially close, like 42-56 and 46-52, so I'm noting those for further contact analysis.

Looking at the emerging pattern, this region seems to form a hairpin structure, with candidate clash zones around 2042/2056, 2046/2052, and 2030/2034/2016. I want to check the side chains in these areas next to confirm the pairing.

Checking glutamate 2042 against lysine 2056's side chain atoms, the distance looks too far given the 6-unit y-offset. Looking at lysine 2041 and leucine 2057, these also seem too distant to clash, so maybe the real issue is backbone atoms in the tight turn rather than side chains. Checking leucine 2046 against valine 2052 gives a CB-CB distance around 5.5, which is fine — no clash there either. I'm now looking at aspartate 2049's side chain oxygens near the turn region to see if that's where the steric conflict actually is.

I'm scanning a tightly packed hydrophobic core region with several residues clustered together around a specific coordinate range, checking coordinates for glutamate 2027, valine 2030, threonine 2031, isoleucine 2033, cysteine 2034, tyrosine 2062, isoleucine 2064, and glutamate 2063 to see if any of their side chain atoms are positioned close enough to cause a genuine steric clash.

Looking at valine 2030's gamma carbon against isoleucine 2064's and cysteine 2034's sulfur, the distances come out around 4 Å, too far to be a clash. Noticing the overall chain path forms three long segments moving up and down in z, suggesting the fold is essentially a three-strand hairpin-like arrangement rather than a compact globular core, which reframes where I should be looking for actual close contacts.

I'm now scanning cross-segment CA-CA distances systematically, comparing early residues in segment one against segment two and three to find any pairs under 10 Å that would indicate real packing interactions, but so far most pairs are landing in the 9.5–11 Å range, too distant to represent side-chain contacts directly.

Continuing to scan distances between segments 1, 2, and 3, checking CA separations around 6-10 Å to spot potential side-chain contacts. So far the closest cross-segment pairs I'm finding are around residues 2018, 2020, and 2026, which seem like the most promising candidates for actual clashes.

Looking more closely at LEU2016's CD1 against VAL2030's CG2, I get a distance around 3.87 Å — a mild but not severe clash. Checking ASN2018's OD1 against SER2026's OG gives about 2.65 Å, which looks more like a favorable hydrogen bond than a clash, and ALA2020 versus VAL2025 also comes back clean at roughly 3.82 Å. Since none of these are true steric violations, I'm now considering that the real clash might be between residues closer in sequence, like positions differing by two.

I'm shifting to look for clashes between residues spaced three or four apart within helical segments, since MolProbity-style contacts often occur that way. I'm scanning the coordinates to find which stretch actually forms a helix by checking CA-CA spacing, and I'm settling on residues 2023 through 2035 as the likely helical region to examine for internal side-chain clashes involving Pro2023 through Glu2035.

I checked several side chain pairs like Thr2028/Leu2029 against Arg2032, but they all seem too far apart to be the culprit, so I'm reconsidering whether the clash is actually a backbone-to-sidechain contact between adjacent residues rather than something more distant. I'm planning to scan more systematically through i, i+2 and i+3 side chain pairs to find where atoms are genuinely close.

Looking at the CA distances across the segment, the stretch from residue 2002 to 2020 spans roughly 53.5 Å over 18 residues, averaging about 3.0 Å per residue, which tells me this region is extended rather than helical, more like a beta strand conformation.

Checking segment 2051-2071 similarly, the CA spacing doesn't match a helix pattern either, so this also looks extended. With three long extended segments sitting roughly 9 Å apart rather than the ~4.8 Å typical of hydrogen-bonded beta strands, I'm wondering if this is part of a beta-solenoid, a polyproline-II arrangement, or perhaps a single chain from a larger fibrous trimer where the other chains aren't shown. Given this extended geometry, I should check for side chain clashes between adjacent segments where residues might point toward each other across that 9 Å gap.

I'm computing tip-to-tip distances between leucine and selenomethionine side chains across seg1 and seg3, but at the z-slices I check, the segments are consistently 7-10 Å apart in a rough triangular arrangement, too far for direct side-chain clashes. This suggests any clashes are more likely happening within a segment (i to i+2 contacts) or in the turn region around 2042-2056 where CA distances drop to about 5 Å, so I want to focus there next.

Looking closer at residues 2040-2056, the CA-CA spacing across pairs like 2042-2056, 2046-2052, and 2047-2051 falls neatly in the 4.6-5.7 Å range, which is a strong signature of an antiparallel β-hairpin. I'm now checking side-chain pairs within this hairpin for actual clashes, comparing leucine, valine, and phenylalanine side-chain atoms across strands, and so far the ones I've checked (2046-2052, 2045-2052) are separated by 5.5 Å or more — not clashing. I'm continuing this check with the 2043-2055 valine-phenylalanine pair.

Now I'm checking the turn region around residues 2048-2051, comparing alanine, aspartate, serine, and lysine side-chain atoms for close contacts — I found a serine OG to aspartate OD1 distance of about 2.78 Å, which looks like a hydrogen bond, and I'm now comparing lysine's CE atom position against serine's CB/OG to see if there's any clash there.

I'm finding a possible C-O overlap of about 2.94 Å between a lysine backbone carbon and a serine oxygen, slightly exceeding their combined van der Waals radii but not severely. Since I'm worried I might be missing the actual worst clash, I'm considering a more systematic approach — bucketing all ~547 atoms by coordinate bins to find close pairs — but that's heavy, so instead I'm thinking about where clashes typically occur in MolProbity-style problems, like side chains of sequentially distant but spatially close residues, or i/i+2 contacts in extended strands where side chains point toward each other.

I'm now checking several i/i+2 residue pairs along an extended segment (LEU2005, ASN2007, ALA2009, ASN2011, etc.), calculating side-chain atom distances like LEU2005 CD2 to ASN2007 OD1/ND2, most of which come out around 3.5-3.8 Å — close but not clearly severe. I'm noting that consecutive CA spacing in this segment is fairly wide (~6.5 Å), which keeps most side-chain contacts moderate, and moving on to check the ASN2006/ILE2008 pair next.

I'm checking if LYS2017's side chain reaches toward the loop near residue 2070, but the distances stay too far for a real clash. I'm now scanning the 2021-2026 region, comparing ASP2021, SER2022, and nearby residues against the 2068-2071 segment to see if any atoms actually overlap.

Since manually comparing 547 atoms pairwise is unwieldy, I'm shifting to a coarser strategy: grouping atoms by residue centroid and residue pairs within close range, then checking those pairs more carefully. I'm going through segment 2 residues around 2036-2041 against segment 3 residues around 2056-2060, measuring distances between side chain atoms like SER2040's OG and LEU2057's CD2, and now comparing the two lysines at 2041 and 2056 to see if their side chains come close enough to clash.

I'm checking a cross-strand hairpin pairing near residues 2042-2055 and 2044-2054, computing CA-CA distances to see which pairs are genuinely close (2044-2054 comes out to about 4.2 Å), and now I'm pulling the backbone and side chain coordinates for SER2044 to compare against ASN2054's side chain atoms in detail.

Looking at SER2044 OG/CB versus ASN2054's OD1 and CG, the closest overlap I find is around 3.06 Å between a carbon and oxygen, which is only a minor 0.16 Å overlap — not severe. Since I haven't found a clash exceeding 0.4 Å yet, I'm broadening my search to check side chain-to-backbone contacts between sequential residues, like a residue's CB against the preceding residue's carbonyl oxygen, starting with ASN2011 against LEU2010, though that pair turns out to be far apart.

I'm now trying a more systematic approach: sorting all atoms by z-coordinate into 3 Å bins so I can check for close pairs within each slice. Going through the bins from z=24-27 down, most nearby atoms belong to sequential residues 2002-2005 and are expected to be close, so nothing alarming there — I'm continuing down through the bins to look for unexpected proximities between non-adjacent residues.

Continuing to trace coordinates for residues 2041 through 2055, checking which side chains and backbone atoms fall near each other in this z 12-15 cluster.

I'm checking a few more distances between nearby atoms - finding NZ to OE1 around 3.03 Å and OG to CE around 2.94 Å, close enough to flag. Now I'm moving to scan the next z-bin (9-12), pulling coordinates for residues 2007, 2008, 2039, and 2040 to check for additional close contacts.

I'm continuing to scan through residue coordinates, checking distances between side chain atoms in the 2040s-2050s range to identify close pairs, then moving into the z 6-9 bin around residues 2008-2010.

I'm continuing to scan coordinates for residues 2049-2060, checking distances between backbone and side-chain atoms to spot potential contacts or hydrogen bonds, then moving into the z 3-6 bin to examine residues around 2009-2010.

I'm checking the distance between residue 2037's beta carbon and selenium in 2060, finding it's within van der Waals contact range, while other atom pairs between these residues are too far apart. Moving to the 0-3 z-range bin, I'm scanning through residues 2011, 2012, 2034, 2035, and 2036 for their coordinates, noting which fall within this slice and which don't.

I continue cataloging coordinates for residues 2037, 2038, 2060, and 2061, then checking specific pairwise distances - CD1 of 2037 to CE and SE of 2060 both come back too far for contact. I also rule out 2033's CG2 and 2034's SG as being outside this z-bin, and find that 2035's OE2 to 2038's CD1 distance of 3.6 Å is borderline but still checking whether this pair falls within van der Waals sum.

I'm now moving into the z -3 to 0 bin, listing atom positions for residues 2011-2013 and 2032-2034 including backbone and side chain atoms, checking a few distances like 2012 CA to potential neighbors before continuing to tabulate coordinates for the arginine at 2032 and the valine/cysteine pair at 2033-2034.

I check a possible hydrogen bond between 2035 OE1 and 2062 OH at about 3.0 Å, then start tallying atom coordinates for residue 2013 in the -6 to -3 z-bin.

Continuing to scan through residues 2014-2033 and 2062, I'm tracking coordinates for backbone and side-chain atoms to look for additional close contacts across this z-range.

I'm continuing to tabulate coordinates for residues 2029 through 2065, tracking their atom positions in the z-bin ranges to check for possible contacts or clashes between nearby side chains.

Continuing to tally residue coordinates in this z-bin, checking which atoms from 2028-2070 fall nearby and could form contacts across this depth slice.

Checking 2029 CD1 against nearby points gives distances too large to matter. Moving into the -15 to -12 z-bin, I'm cataloging candidates like 2018 C, O and 2019 N for closer distance checks.

Still recording atomic coordinates...
